clue.text: Cook is employed by Scottish bank

indicators.note: the word is is taken on, placed inside, the Scottish bank

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef finds a job with a bank north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is a brae, a hillside; 'is employed by' puts IS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is a way to cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: Abruptly end holiday —- ring following the onset of 'flu

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
the letter O is ring-shaped
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A holiday cut short when flu strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: To break off a talk or relationship is to end it suddenly.

clue.text: Section of curve in semicircular canal

indicators.note: signals the answer is hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of the curved semicircular canal of the inner ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a part of a curve, such as part of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Chief, first to size up regiment

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of size

parts.note: taken as written
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: The commander is the first to measure up the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or authority, as chief does.

clue.text: Frustrated editor's on whisky

indicators.note: in a down-style reading, one piece placed on, following, another: the editor comes after the whisky

parts.note: Scotch is whisky from Scotland
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An editor, thwarted at work, has turned to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to thwart or put an end to it, so a scotched scheme has been frustrated.

clue.text: One who's given the odd role?

definitions.text: One who's given the odd role?

parts.words: One who's given the odd role?
parts.note: an odd role is a quirky, eccentric part; the performer who specialises in such distinctive supporting parts

explanation.definitionFit: This performer specialises in playing unusual or eccentric supporting characters rather than leads.

clue.text: Fix match in advance

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
money paid down is paid in advance, as a down payment

explanation.surface: Someone rigs the result of a game beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests match-fixing; 'Fix' is the definition and the rest is a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to secure or fasten something firmly in place.

clue.text: Satisfactory compromise pleased spiritualist

parts.note: happy means pleased
a medium is a spiritualist who claims to contact the dead

explanation.surface: A contented psychic has found a sensible middle way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a satisfying balance between two extremes.

clue.text: How I was finished with writing? Not in that case

definitions.text: How I was finished with writing? Not in that case

parts.words: How I was finished with writing? Not in that case
parts.note: a handwritten small i ends with a point above it, but a capital letter, in the upper case, gets no point

explanation.definitionFit: A small letter i is completed with a dot over it, while the capital form has none.

clue.text: Warm yellow coat sorely needed?

parts.note: a warming yellow paste spread like a coating on a sore part of the body as an old remedy

explanation.definitionFit: This old remedy was a poultice of mustard paste applied to the chest or sore muscles for warmth.

clue.text: New limits within EU — overdue, to sum up

indicators.note: says the new limits sit inside the two letters EU

parts.note: taken as written, the European Union
caps are upper limits, as on spending
late means behind time, overdue

explanation.surface: Fresh ceilings on European Union spending have arrived late, in summary.
explanation.definitionFit: To encapsulate something is to express its essence briefly, a synonym for summarise.

clue.text: About to dump in mine

indicators.note: here signals turning round, so the word meaning dump is read backwards

parts.note: to tip rubbish is to dump it

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of dumping waste down a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is the reversal signal and 'to dump' is TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a coal mine, the shaft and workings dug underground.

clue.text: Set upset by lament that's most sensitive

indicators.note: means beside, so the rearranged set comes next to the lament

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to lament

indicators.note: the three letters of set are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A grieving song disturbs someone who is highly sensitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen senses are acute ones, so the keenest is the most acutely sensitive.

clue.text: Real gent has to be flexible about servants getting increase

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the servants
the letters of real gent must bend into a new order

parts.note: men can mean manservants or male workers

explanation.surface: A gentleman must bend to the staff who want a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be flexible' turns REAL GENT into ENLARGET, and 'about' puts MEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is an increase in size, as of a photograph.

clue.text: Assistant in a small company, reportedly lacking sufficient weight

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: tells us the word for underweight is only heard, and is spelt differently

parts.note: light means not heavy enough, underweight

explanation.surface: A junior helper in a small firm is said to be a lightweight.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or attendant, originally one who helps a priest at the altar.

clue.text: By implication, ESP centre might be shown up by such deception

parts.note: these nine letters are a falsified, rearranged form of the word pretences

explanation.surface: A centre for extrasensory perception would be exposed as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer says 'PRETENCES, made false (rearranged)', which gives ESP CENTRE; so the clue phrase is what the answer would build.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining something by deceit is the legal sense, so the phrase names a kind of trickery.

clue.text: Find out about unusual forms sensitive to some radiation

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes round the word for unusual
says the letters of find are thrown out of order

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: Discover what odd shapes are picked up by special sensors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' is only a link here; 'out' makes INFD, which 'about' wraps around the unusual word.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared cameras and film respond to radiation beyond the red end of the visible spectrum.

clue.text: Exile in carriage

definitions.meaning: convicts were exiled by being shipped to penal colonies
the conveying of goods or people from place to place

explanation.surface: An exile travels in a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both conveyance of goods and the historical punishment of deporting convicts overseas.

clue.text: PC turned over college flat

indicators.note: the college name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Eton College is the English public school
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A police constable turns over a student flat.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable searching a flat, but it is a personal computer; ETON is the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a small portable personal computer, so it is one kind of PC.

clue.text: Unpaid article on struggling RU team

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of what follows

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the letters of RU team flounder into a new order

explanation.surface: A struggling rugby union side is unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union, which was famously amateur until 1995.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is unpaid, playing for love rather than money.

clue.text: The home of the brave?

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, so his dwelling is a domed tent; the phrase also echoes the US anthem

explanation.definitionFit: This domed tent-like dwelling was home to some Native American peoples, whose warriors were called braves.

clue.text: A disinclination to act in opening of Educating Rita, possibly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of the next word
says the name Rita may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Inertia shown at the start of the play Educating Rita.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play and film; 'possibly' turns RITA into RTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia in people is sluggishness, a reluctance to move or do anything.

clue.text: One playing with snake in playground backed to get hurt

indicators.note: the reversed playground receives the hurt inside it
the word for playground is turned backwards

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a playground
to harm is to hurt

explanation.surface: A child playing with a snake in the park is about to be bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in playground' tempts you to look for a hidden word; 'backed' gives CER, which 'to get' fills with the hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake charmer plays a pipe to a snake, apparently making it sway.

clue.text: Had on? Runs off in misery

indicators.note: says the runs are taken away from the word before

parts.note: you wore clothes when you had them on
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Wearing something that comes off at a run leaves one wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is great sorrow or distress, a literary synonym for misery.

clue.text: Set up, he got drunk in golf club

indicators.note: says the jumbled letters sit inside the golf club

parts.note: a putter is the club used on the green

indicators.note: the letters of he got are reeling into another order

explanation.surface: A golfer got drunk at the golf club and was set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' looks like a clubhouse but is the club itself; 'drunk' makes OGETH, which 'in' places between its first four and last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a structure or plan is to assemble it, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: The man's carrying round a gardening implement

indicators.note: the pronoun holds the round letter inside it

parts.note: he is the man; the 's stands for is
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: A man is carrying a gardening tool around.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding and breaking up soil.

clue.text: Spanish sportsmen at a party held by wife?

indicators.note: the run of short words is held inside the title for a wife

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Spanish athletes at a party with their wives in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadors are bullfighters, the men who kill the bull in Spanish bullfighting.

clue.text: Father's one close pal

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
I is the Roman numeral for one
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A priest's one intimate companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend, an informal synonym.
